questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The speed of light $\left(c\right)$, gravitational constant $\left(\text{G}\right)$ and Planck’s constant $\left(h\right)$ are taken as fundamental units in a system. The dimensions of time in this new system should be:
questions.solution:
Let time, $T ∝ c^{X} G^{Y} h^{Z}$

$⇒ T = kc^{X} G^{Y} h^{Z}$

Taking dimensions on both sides

$[ M^{0} L^{0} T^{1} ] = {[ LT^{- 1} ]}^{X} {[ M^{- 1} L^{3} T^{- 2} ]}^{Y} {[ ML^{2} T^{- 1} ]}^{Z}$

i.e.,

$[ M^{0} L^{0} T^{1} ] = [ M^{- Y + Z} L^{X + 3Y + 2Z} T^{- X - 2Y - Z} ]$

Equating powers of $M, L$, and $T$, on both sides, we get –

$- Y + Z = 0... ( 1 )$

$X + 3Y + 2Z = 0... ( 2 )$

$- X - 2Y - Z = 1... ( 3 )$

From equation (i)

Adding (2) and (3)

$Y + Z = 1$

or $2Y = 1( ∵ Z = Y )$

$∴ Z = Y = \dfrac{1}{2}$

Putting these values in (2), we get –

$X + \dfrac{3}{2} + 1 = 0orX = \dfrac{- 5}{2}$

Hence, $[ T ] = [ G^{\dfrac{1}{2}} h^{\dfrac{1}{2}} c^{\dfrac{- 5}{2}} ]$

questions.q: If the error in the measurement of momentum is $20 %$, then the error in the calculation of kinetic energy is (assume the error in measurement of $m$ as zero)&
questions.solution:
$KE = \dfrac{1}{2}\dfrac{p2}{m}$

${p}_{1} = \dfrac{6}{5}p$

${KE}_{2} = \dfrac{1}{2}\left(\dfrac{36}{25}\right)\dfrac{p2}{m}$

$= \dfrac{1}{2} \left[\dfrac{ \left(\dfrac{6}{5}$ p\right)^{2} - p^{2}}{m}\right]

$= \dfrac{11}{25}\dfrac{p2}{m}$

Percentage change in kinetic energy $= \dfrac{ΔKE}{KE1} \times100$

$= \dfrac{11}{25} \times100 = 44%$

questions.q: Number of particles, given by $n = - D\dfrac{{n}_{2} - {n}_{1}}{{x}_{2} - {x}_{1}}$, is crossing a unit area perpendicular to $x$-axis in unit time, where ${n}_{1}$ and ${n}_{2}$ are number of particles per unit volume for the value of $x$ meant to ${x}_{2}$ and ${x}_{1}$. questions.solution:
Given, number of particle passing from unit area in unit time $= n$

$= \dfrac{Numberofparticle}{A \times t} = \dfrac{\left[{M}^{0}{L}^{0}{T}^{0}\right]}{\left[{L}^{2}\right]\left[T\right]$} = $\left[{L}^{- 2}{T}^{- 1}\right]$

$\left[{n}_{1}\right] = \left[{n}_{2}\right] = Numberofparticleinunitvolume = \left[{L}^{- 3}\right]

Now,$ from $the given formula \left[D\right] = \dfrac{\left[n\right]\left[{x}_{2} - {x}_{1}\right]}{\left[{n}_{2} - {n}_{1}\right]}$

$= \dfrac{\left[{L}^{- 2}{T}^{- 1}\right]\left[L\right]}{\left[{L}^{- 3}\right]}$

$= \left[{L}^{2}{T}^{- 1}\right]$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A spherical liquid drop is placed on a horizontal plane. A small disturbance causes the volume of the drop to oscillate. The time period of oscillation $\left(T\right)$ of the liquid drop depends on the radius $( r )$ of the drop, density $\left(ρ\right)$ and surface tension $\left(S\right)$ of the liquid. Which among the following will be a possible expression for the time period? where~$k$& is a dimensionless constant.
questions.solution:
According to the question,

time period, $T ∝ r^{a}{ρ}^{b}S^{c}$

$T = kr^{a}{ρ}^{b}S^{c}$ ..... (i)

Thus, putting dimension, we get

$[ T ] = {[ L ]}^{a} {[ ML^{- 3} ]}^{b} {[ MT^{- 2} ]}^{c}$

$\left[T\right] = {\left[M\right]}^{b + c} ⋅ {\left[L\right]}^{a - 3b} ⋅ {\left[T\right]}^{- 2c}$

Equating the dimensions of both sides, we get

$b + c = 0, a - 3b = 0$

and $- 2c = 1$

$∴ c = - \dfrac{1}{2}$

$∴ b = \dfrac{1}{2}$

and $a = 3b = \dfrac{3}{2}$

Putting these value of $a, b and c$ into Equation. (i), we get

$T = k ⋅ r^{\dfrac{3}{2}}{ρ}^{\dfrac{1}{2}} ⋅ S^{- \dfrac{1}{2}}$

$= k\sqrt{\dfrac{ρ}{S}r^{3}}$

Stefan's law is $E = \sigma ( T^{4} )⇒\sigma = \dfrac{E}{T^{4}}$

where, $E =\dfrac{\text{Energy}}{\text{Area} \times \text{Time}}= \dfrac{Watt}{m\text{2}}$

$\sigma = \dfrac{\text{Watt-}m^{- 2}}{K4} = Wm^{- 2}K^{- 4}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
A screw gauge gives the following reading when used to measure the diameter of a wire.

Main scale reading : $0$ mm

Circular scale reading: $52$ divisions

Given that $1$ mm on the main scale corresponds to

100 divisions of the circular scale.

The diameter of the wire from the above data is
questions.solution:
Diameter of wire,

$d = MSR + CSR \times LC$

$= 0 + 52 \times \dfrac{1}{100}$

$= 0.52mm = 0.052cm.$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: In a vernier calliper $N$ divisions of vernier scale coincides with$ \text{ and } ( N - 1 )$ divisions of the main scale (in which length of one division is $1$ mm). The least count of the instrument should be (in $cm$):
questions.solution:
Least count $1MSD - 1VSD$

$= 1MSD - ( \dfrac{N - 1}{N} )MSD$

$∵ NVSD = ( N - 1 )MSD$

$∴ 1VSD = ( \dfrac{N - 1}{N} )MSD$

$∴$ Least count $= \dfrac{1}{N} MSD = ( \dfrac{1}{N} ) \times ( \dfrac{1}{10} )cm = ( \dfrac{1}{10N} )$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: If the speed of light $( c )$, acceleration due to gravity $( g )$ and pressure $( p )$ are taken as the fundamental quantities, then the dimension of gravitational constant is
questions.solution:
Let $[ G ] ∝ c^{x} g^{y} p^{z}$

by substituting the following dimensions :

$[ G ] = [ M^{- 1}L^{3}T^{- 2} ] , [ c ] = [ {LT}^{- 1} ] , [ g ] = [ {LT}^{- 2} ]$

$[ p ] = [ {ML}^{- 1}T^{- 2} ]$

and by comparing the powers of both sides we can get $x = 0, y = 2, z = - 1$
∴ $[ G ] ∝ c^{0} g^{2} p^{- 1}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: In the density measurement of a cube, the mass and edge length are measured as $\left(10.00 \pm 0.10\right)kg$ and $\left(0.10 \pm 0.01\right)m,$ respectively. The error in the measurement of density is:
questions.solution:
Density $\left(ρ\right) = \dfrac{mass}{volume}$
$\dfrac{∆ ρ}{ρ} = \dfrac{∆ m}{m} + \dfrac{∆ V}{V}$
$= \dfrac{∆ m}{m} + \dfrac{3 ∆ a}{a} \left(∵ V = a^{3}\right)
$= $\dfrac{0.1}{10} +$3 $\left(\dfrac{0.01}{0.1}\right)$
$= 0.01 + 3 \left(0.1\right)
$= 0.31

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The dimensional formula of& Planck’s constant is
questions.solution:
According to Planck:
$E = hv$
$h = \dfrac{E}{v}$
Substituting the dimensions of known physical quantities:
$\begin{array}{ll}[ h ] = \dfrac{[ ML^{2} T^{- 2} ]}{[ T^{- 1} ]} \\ or[ h ] = ML^{2} T^{- 1}\end{array}$
So, SI unit or Planck’s constant is kg m2s–1 which can also be written as
$( kgm^{2} s^{- 2} ) \times s$ . But as $kgm^{2} s^{- 2}$ is joule, so unit of h is $joule \times sec$ , i.e., Js.

questions.q: The resistance $R = \dfrac{V}{I}$, where $V = ( 100 \pm 5 ) V$ and $I = \left(10 \pm 0.2\right)A$. The maximum percentage error in $R$ is
questions.solution:
Given, $V = \left(100 \pm 5\right)V ⇒ ∆ V = 5V$

$I = \left(10 \pm 0.2\right)A ⇒ ∆ I = 0.2A$

$R = \dfrac{V}{I}$

$\dfrac{∆ R}{R} = \dfrac{∆ V}{V} + \dfrac{∆ I}{I}$

$= \dfrac{5}{100} + \dfrac{0.2}{10} = 0.05 + 0.02$

$= 0.07$

$= 7%$
